- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes in history.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag or failure to capture near-term downward pressure.
- Overreacts to recent high values (overshoots after spikes), then fails to correct downward quickly.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast, particularly when history includes a recent peak.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds onto high forecasts longer than observed price behavior suggests.
- Tends to underestimate volatility in the final 10 days, leading to overly optimistic low forecasts.
- Sensitive to recent low values — when history includes a recent dip, model often fails to anticipate a rebound or underestimates recovery speed.
